column4: The section describes the city as shaped by those who dwell there and cites a prayer for its safety in 2:126; this ayah shows Abraham and Ishmael raising the House's foundations, making the sanctuary's human construction part of that place.

The section cites fear that following guidance could mean being snatched from one's land, answered by a secure sanctuary; this ayah recalls believers fearing people would snatch them from the land until God gave them shelter, help and provision.

The section's root note B002 glosses س ك ن as dwelling in a house; this ayah says people settled in the homes of those who wronged themselves and saw what befell them, making a dwelling both shelter and a warning from its former residents.
The section presents the city as a place of security and habitation; this ayah says the people carved secure houses in the mountains, while 15:83 completes the scene with a sudden blast.
The section makes sanctuary a place of protection; this ayah says God repels some people by others so houses where His name is mentioned will not be demolished, showing what protection preserves.

The section describes a city through its residents and their staying; this ayah recalls towns destroyed for wrongdoing, with abandoned wells and lofty palaces, showing settled places emptied by punishment.
The section's root note for miskin links س ك ن to dwelling; this ayah says God made homes a place of rest and also made portable shelters, connecting settling to the shelter that lets people remain.
The section's Meccan sanctuary is a place of protection; this ayah condemns those who bar God's mosques and seek their ruin, saying their entry is only in fear, the reverse of a safe sacred place.

The section develops the difference between protection inside the sanctuary and exposure outside it; this ayah calls fighting in a sacred month grave but also names barring people from the Sacred Mosque and expelling them, exposing violations of that boundary.
The section centers a city and its people; this ayah describes a blessed Book sent to warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, extending the city's relation to its surrounding region.
The section treats a sacred place as shaped by those who inhabit and guard it; this ayah disqualifies polytheists from maintaining God's mosques, while 9:18 names the believers who may maintain them.

The section says a city takes its character from its residents; this ayah gives maintenance of God's mosques to those who believe, pray, give charity and fear God, specifying the community that tends the sacred place.

The section joins sanctuary, visitors and provision; this ayah names watering pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque, then distinguishes those services from belief and striving, adding the work that sustains a pilgrimage center.
The section's root note B002 connects miskin with dwelling; this ayah promises believers good dwellings in the Gardens of Eden, giving the word-family a lasting abode as well as an earthly one.
The section says residents shape the city they inhabit; this ayah says God would not destroy towns unjustly while their people were reforming, tying a town's fate to its residents' conduct.
The section's secure-city scene has a contrary end when punishment arrives; after 15:82's secure carved homes, this ayah says a blast seized their people in the morning.

The section says a city is affected by the people who settle in it and names punishment that descends; this ayah says a town's affluent residents disobeyed before it was destroyed, making the inhabitants' conduct the cause of the reversal.
The section opens with the Messenger present in the city; this ayah says his opponents nearly drove him from the land, placing his stay in the city beside the threat of expulsion.

The section links the sanctuary and sacrificial signs to the approach to God; this ayah says honoring God's rites comes from hearts' piety, clarifying the inward reverence that gives those visible boundaries meaning.

The section discusses hady and qurbān as offerings and provision; this ayah says every community has a rite for mentioning God over livestock He provided, placing the Meccan offering among a wider pattern of worship.

The section describes a person without protection and another seeking refuge; this ayah gives the wronged permission to defend themselves, and 22:40 adds that they were expelled from homes and explains the protection of worship places.

The section joins a safe place to worship of its Lord; this promise says God will establish believers in the land and replace their fear with security so they may worship Him, making safety a condition of settled worship.

The section cites the fear of following guidance in 28:57; this preceding ayah says the Messenger cannot guide whom he loves but God guides whom He wills, framing the concern that the next ayah answers with a secure sanctuary.
The section joins a settled town to safety and provision; this ayah describes blessed towns placed along a route and travel between them by night and day in safety.

The section's image holds settlement beside movement between places; after 34:18's safe route between towns, this ayah says the people asked for longer distances between journeys and were scattered, reversing connected settlement into dispersal.
The section centers the city and its people; this ayah says the Arabic revelation warns the Mother of Cities and those around it, making the city a center whose warning reaches beyond its boundary.

The section names the truce as a relation between enemies and discusses who has protection; this ayah says kindness and justice remain permitted toward those who neither fight believers nor expel them from their homes, setting a boundary for peaceful relations.

The section describes a person outside protection and a city that can shelter or expose its residents; this ayah names those who fought believers, expelled them from their homes, or helped expel them as the boundary for alliance.
The section's root note B002 links س ك ن to dwelling; this ayah promises good dwellings in the Gardens of Eden alongside salvation, repeating the enduring-home sense.

The section defines the city as a bounded place shaped by residents and their staying; this ayah says Thamud were settled in the land and made palaces on its plains and houses in its mountains, showing people forming their inhabited landscape.
The section ties the miskin's ability to remain somewhere to provision; this ayah condemns people who do not urge one another to feed the needy, showing the failure to sustain the poor resident.

The section presents the city as a community formed by its inhabitants; this ayah names Quraysh, while 106:2-4 specify their seasonal journeys, the House, food and safety, identifying the community behind the city image.
